PullRequest.Title: Reject file URIs with the drive letter as host name in add_artifact_or_reference
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347338

Agents on Windows sometimes record a file with `add_artifact_or_reference` using two slashes, for example `file://D:/repo/plan.md`. That parses with `D:` as the host name and names a network path, so the recorded entry pointed to a file that does not exist.

`add_artifact_or_reference` now rejects a `file` URI whose host name is a drive letter, like it already rejects plain file system paths, and the error names the corrected URI with three slashes (`file:///D:/repo/plan.md`), so the agent can retry right away.

A test covers the rejection and the suggested URI.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add a valid file or resource artifact/reference, including a realistic batched tool call
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each submitted item is synchronously validated before the per-session mutation queue; a changed file URI performs one anchored authority check after the URI parse that already existed. The batch then enters the existing mutation/persistence path once.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the merged session artifact collection via _persistOrderedListVisibleSessionState.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one persistence operation for a successful batch mutation, regardless of the number of submitted entries; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A successful valid batch followed the same single serialized persistence path before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The durable write is awaited before publication and tool completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of entries in the submitted batch. URI parsing remains once per file/resource item; the diff adds one regex check only for file-scheme items, so validation remains linear in batch size and URI text length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Validation is synchronous within one tool invocation. Mutations and durable writes remain serialized by session through SequencerByKey; the diff adds no parallel work or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in URI validation. Cold and warm behavior are identical, with no changed cache key, miss retry, coalescing, or retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the changed hunk and sole production caller show one additional in-process regex test per valid file URI and no new boundary operation, retained state, scheduling, or repeated parse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact URI and batch sizes vary, but realistic calls are small and the added anchored check is bounded by the already parsed authority text; this does not create a material performance mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added validation is minor synchronous work proportional to the existing per-item URI parsing and does not change persistence cardinality or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reject a two-slash Windows drive file URI such as file://D:/repo/report.md
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The input is parsed and the new authority guard throws during batch validation, before entering SessionArtifacts.mutate or any persistence operation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Items validated before the first malformed entry in the batch; processing stops at the malformed URI. The new error text is allocated once for the rejected call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous validation only; the rejected call never enters the per-session sequencer and starts no asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or populated. Repeated invalid agent retries repeat only bounded parsing and validation, while each retry previously could proceed to mutation/persistence.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: requireUri throws before parseSessionArtifactInputs returns, and execute invokes mutate only after all inputs validate.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent retry frequency is unknown, but the changed path removes rather than adds the durable-write boundary for this malformed input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Compared with the pre-diff behavior, the malformed URI is rejected before the existing filesystem-backed persistence path, reducing work and avoiding retained artifact state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the added artifact-server unit test
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test creates an in-memory harness, executes one malformed add call, and asserts rejection and an empty collection; no production startup, render, input, or long-lived path is affected.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional test case with one item per test-suite execution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited test invocation; no changed product concurrency.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete changed test hunk and harness implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Test runner overhead is not material to product performance.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the add-artifact validation through batching, per-session sequencing, persistence, and tests. The production change retains the existing URI parse, adds only a bounded authority check for file URIs, and rejects the targeted malformed input before mutation and durable persistence. No actionable performance finding or regression-fix learning signal was identified.
